summary.text: Case 1 was a 67-year-old male diagnosed with nodular basal cell carcinoma of the areola, a lesion on the nipple-areola complex. The table records a prior non-melanoma skin cancer count of 5 and no history of immunosuppression, solid organ malignancy, autoimmune disease or chest or breast surgery or radiation.

The patient underwent Mohs micrographic surgery, with a preoperative lesion size of 10 mm, a postoperative defect size of 20 mm and a final surgical margin of 10 mm. 3 stages were needed for a histologically clear margin. The final surgical length and type of repair were 3.4 cm (CLC), with sutures as the repair material. No complications and no recurrence were noted. Follow-up with dermatology was 81 months and follow-up at UCSD was 84 months.

summary.text: Case 7 was a 59-year-old male diagnosed with nodular basal cell carcinoma of the areola and nipple, a lesion on the nipple-areola complex. The table records a prior non-melanoma skin cancer count of 1 and no history of immunosuppression, solid organ malignancy, autoimmune disease or chest or breast surgery or radiation.

The patient underwent Mohs micrographic surgery, with a preoperative lesion size of 11 mm, a postoperative defect size of 47 mm and a final surgical margin of 36 mm. 4 stages were needed for a histologically clear margin. The final surgical length and type of repair were 0.5 cm^(2) (C-V transposition flap); 8 cm (CLC), with sutures as the repair material. No complications and no recurrence were noted. Follow-up with dermatology was 36 months and follow-up at UCSD was 45 months.
